subject: MSA: IP allocation and productization — redlines + signature flow
messages:
From: Amir Rahman <amir.rahman@nebula-analytics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@nebula-analytics.com, sana@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Nebula MSA redlines (IP allocation + productization asks)

Kimberly,

Thanks for the call today — attached is our redlined MSA (PDF) with comments focused on Sections 6 and 9 (IP/Feedback). Two key asks from our side:

1) Nebula must retain ownership of customer-contributed prompts & outputs that are either productized or embedded into our models.
2) We can accept a narrow non-exclusive license for Redwood to use outputs for improving hosted model performance, but only with explicit opt-in and audit evidence.

We flagged telemetry and evidence requirements under the audit/training section — our legal team (cc'd) will follow up with specifics.

Can your team confirm Redwood's preferred language for:
- assignment vs license on productized outputs,
- permitted training data usage and retention windows,
- feedback license scope (telemetry vs content).

We'd like to get to a signature-ready MSA by EOW if possible — happy to hop on another 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

Attachments: Nebula_MSA_redline_20260602.pdf

Best,
Amir Rahman
Head of Legal Operations
Nebula Analytics

Amir — thanks for the redline and the clear priorities. Looping in Kar?thik (legal) and Ben (account lead) to coordinate. We can move quickly but need to align internally on two things you called out: assignment vs license on productized outputs, and the audit/evidence path for any training opt-in.

Proposed next steps:
- Kar?thik will annotate the redline with counterlanguage by EOD.
- Ben and I will review commercial impact and confirm whether we can sign off on an opt-in training flow with an evidence package tied to SOC2 + telemetry logs.
- If we land on language, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope for mutual signature and a short SOW addendum for productization concessions.

Can you confirm whether Nebula requires a perpetual assignment for all outputs that are productized, or assignment only for outputs that are embedded into Nebula-owned models/services? That distinction will affect how we draft the fallbacks.

Thanks — Kim

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Amir Rahman <amir.rahman@nebula-analytics.com>, legal@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula MSA redlines (IP allocation + productization asks)

Kim / team — I reviewed Nebula's redline and attached an annotated MSA with suggested compromise language (see PDF). High-level positions and suggested edits below:

1) Productized outputs: we should avoid broad assignment. Proposed compromise: customer retains ownership; customer grants Redwood a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use customer outputs solely to provide Redwood's services and to enable Nebula-specific integrations. For productization (customer-built products that embed Redwood output), the parties can negotiate a separate commercial annex.

2) Training & data use: Nebula requests opt-in + auditability. We can accept an opt-in model for training where customer explicitly flags datasets for training and Redwood agrees to provide a verifiable evidence package (hashes and retention log entries) and a maximum retention window of 90 days for training material used in model updates unless a longer period is mutually agreed.

3) Feedback license / telemetry: clarify telemetry as aggregated/anonymous for platform improvements. For content-level feedback (customer-provided prompts + outputs), we propose a scoped license limited to debugging, quality improvements, and model safety; productization rights require separate consent.

4) Evidence and SOC2: ask Nebula to provide the SOC2 report (or bridge letter) and access to an evidence upload location (we will share a secure S3 bucket link). We'll codify a request-response SLA for evidence requests.

I attached Annotated_MSA_kiyer_20260603.pdf with line edits. If these positions look acceptable to Nebula, ask them to mark acceptance or propose exact redline text in the PDF and we can take to DocuSign.

— Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Annotated_MSA_kiyer_20260603.pdf
From: Amir Rahman <amir.rahman@nebula-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, legal@nebula-analytics.com, sana@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula MSA redlines (IP allocation + productization asks)

Karthik / Kim — appreciate the quick read and concrete suggestions. A couple clarifications from our side: we will not agree to any language that could be read as giving Redwood a perpetual license to productize customer outputs without explicit commercial terms. The suggested scoped license for debugging/quality is reasonable, but we need explicit carveouts:

- No assignment or implied transfer of ownership for outputs used to build Nebula-facing products.
- Any use of outputs for model training beyond short-term debugging requires an executed training addendum and a monthly evidence bundle.

On SOC2: we'll share our Type II report under an NDA (we'll upload to the S3 link once the NDA is in place). We can accept the 90-day retention baseline for flagged training material, but only if audit logs include request IDs and vector/hash evidence for each file used.

We will do a 30-min legal ops sync tomorrow at 10am PT to line up final redline language. After that we'd expect to exchange a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

— Amir

- I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope with the MSA + training addendum placeholders once language is agreed.
- Ben to confirm commercial annex language for any productization clause (if Nebula later requests assignment-like terms).

- Provide sample evidence fields you require (we'll capture hashes/request IDs in the evidence bundle).

If we get sign-off in the sync, target to have a DocuSign envelope out the same day and fully executed within 72 hours. If anything changes on timing, flag to me directly.

Thanks — Kim
